## 8 days of birdwatching in Suriname

One of the main targets of the trip is the Guianan cock-of-the-rock. We look for it in humid forests along the Saramacca River. The males stand out for their bright orange plumage and large, semicircular crests.

At Weg Naar Zee, you can watch scarlet ibises along the coast. Large flocks fly over the shoreline and mangroves, a particularly striking sight in the evening light.

Night outings offer a chance to see and hear forest wildlife that is hard to spot by day. The programme includes looking for forest owls and other nocturnal birds.

You spend several days at Peperpot Nature Park. Tropical forest has gradually reclaimed the old plantation canals and avenues, making this historic landscape a good place to watch birds and other wildlife.

The Saramacca River flows through extensive forests in central Suriname. Zintete Lodge sits on its banks, far from settlements and roads, making it easy to start birdwatching just after dawn.

From savanna and dense forest to river valleys and the coast, the variety of habitats lets you see a wide range of birds on a single trip.
